requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: Stops the type-collection code that the analyzer shares from throwing on bad key contracts, and adds tests and docs for types that use `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`. In `TypeCollector`, when a member mixes int and string keys, the diagnostic is still reported and the member is now skipped. Duplicate int or string keys no longer hit `Dictionary.Add` twice, so the analyzer no longer crashes. The same edits are made in both member loops (properties and fields). The change also makes `MessagePackObjectAttribute.KeyAsPropertyName` settable, which is a public API change.
story.why: Issue 2234 says analyzer diagnostics stop appearing for suppressed types from 3.1.1 onward. The fix assumes the analyzer was failing, likely with a thrown exception, while collecting members. The new analyzer tests check that MsgPack004, 003, 015 and 005 are reported for suppressed types. They also check that MsgPack011, 016 and 017 are not.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack.Annotations/Attributes.cs: `KeyAsPropertyName` gains a public setter. Nothing in the requirement or the other changes needs it, and static check S3 fails on it.
README.md: new section documenting analyzer behaviour for suppressed types, including a MsgPack012 claim that no test covers.
The duplicate-key and mixed-key guards also change behaviour for ordinary, non-suppressed types (one test covers this for the property loop).
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The guards clearly prevent `Dictionary.Add` from throwing on duplicate keys, and the tests exercise the property loop. The diff does not show anything specific to `SuppressSourceGeneration`, so it is unclear whether these crash guards are the actual root cause of the issue. The field loop (L1148–1182) has no duplicate-key or mixed-key test. The `KeyAsPropertyName` setter is unrelated and needs an owner decision.

findings.description: Nothing in the diff is specific to `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The changes only guard against crashes on duplicate or mixed keys. If the 3.1.1 regression was that suppressed types are skipped elsewhere (for example, an early return in the analyzer), this diff does not address it. The new tests MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported would pass only if that path already works. Check whether those tests failed before this change.
The field-loop guards (L1148, L1163–1166, L1179–1182) are not exercised by any test. All duplicate-key and mixed-key tests use properties.

The new `continue` skips the rest of the loop body for a mixed-key member. This includes the formatter-attribute lookup (L1045) and any per-member type checks that follow. Further diagnostics such as MsgPack003 on that member may silently disappear. The same applies at L1148.
Adds a public setter to `KeyAsPropertyName`, which is unrelated to the bug. It is a public API surface change in the shipped Annotations assembly (S3 fails).

Adding a public setter to MessagePackObjectAttribute.KeyAsPropertyName allows callers to write [MessagePackObject(KeyAsPropertyName = true)]. Because MessagePackObjectAttribute already has constructor MessagePackObjectAttribute(bool keyAsPropertyName = false), Roslyn AttributeData will record ConstructorArguments[0] as false and place KeyAsPropertyName = true in NamedArguments, but no code in MessagePack.SourceGenerator was updated to inspect NamedArguments for KeyAsPropertyName (previously impossible when the property was get-only) and no test covers named-argument usage, risking false MsgPack004 diagnostics and generator/runtime mismatch.
